findings.F1_pre_existing_hashseed_nondeterminism: The Amulet Titan goldfish APL and the Boros Energy match APL exhibit cross-process nondeterminism NOT controlled by the RNG seed (default PYTHONHASHSEED, and for Boros even with PYTHONHASHSEED=0 -- id()-based ordering). SAME unchanged source produced Amulet 5.76 vs 5.98 and Boros 39-55 a_wins across repeated runs. This is PRE-EXISTING (reproduces at the R2 branch-point with R2 absent), NOT introduced by R2. Consequence: 'bit-identical' goldfish/match NR is only well-defined with a pinned hash seed (Amulet) and is undefined run-to-run for Boros (id-ordering). Bit-identity for R2 was therefore proven on DETERMINISTIC decks (Golgari Control, UW Control exercise) plus fixed-hashseed goldfish. RECOMMEND: open an IMPERFECTIONS entry for the Amulet/Boros APL ordering nondeterminism; the design's NR-1 named Boros mirror, which is not a valid bit-identity discriminator at the process level.
findings.F2_design_baseline_note: Amulet goldfish here is n=50 (5.98 / median 6); the design's locked NR-3 baseline is n>=large (T7.11 / median 7). These are NOT compared -- what is proven is cross-revision IDENTITY at n=50, seed=42, which is what the task requested.
